text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 19 in history.
1154 - Henry II crowned as King of England; his great achievement was to strengthen the administration of the country and to establish the Exchequer.
1564 - The battle of Dreux took place when Catholics under de Guise defeated the Huguenots in the first French Religious War.
1741 - Vitus Bering, Danish born explorer died of scurvy; . he gave his name to the Bering Sea and Bering Strait and discovered Alaska.
1793 - In the French Revolutionary wars, French forces under General Dugommier and Napoleon Bonaparte re-captured the city of Toulon from the English.
1848 - British poet and writer Emily Bronte, famed for her novel "Wuthering Heights", died.
1851 - Joseph Mallord William Turner, English artist, died. One of the greatest landscape painters whose use of light anticipated French impressionism.
1863 - Linoleum, the smooth floor-covering, was patented by Frederick Walton of London.
1888 - Orchestral conductor Fritz Reiner born in Hungary; he led the Chicago Symphony Orchestra and made many famous recordings, especially of Strauss and Bartok.
1902 - British actor Sir Ralph Richardson born.
1906 - Leonid Brezhnev born; Soviet president from 1960 and leader from 1964, he expanded the military machine and was also an architect of detente.
1910 - French writer Jean Genet born; best known for his novels "Miracle de la Rose" and "Notre-Dames des Fleurs".

1915 - Edith Piaf, French singer, born as Edith Giovanna Gassion. Known as the "Little Sparrow", she became legendary for her sad and nostalgic songs including "La Vie en Rose" and "Non, je ne regrette rien".
1939 - The German cruise liner Columbus was scuttled by its crew in the Atlantic after being followed by a U.S. cruiser; 577 survivors were picked up.
1941 - Adolf Hitler took over as commander-in-chief of the army after sacking Field Marshal von Brauchitsch.
1944 - Richard Leakey born. A paleontologist and environmentalist, he led a single-handed crusade against poaching and wildlife land abuse in Kenya.
1957 - An agreement was signed to start a regular air service between Moscow and London.
1965 - Charles de Gaulle won 54.5 percent of the vote in the second and concluding round of the French presidential election, defeating Francois Mitterrand.
1981 - The eight-strong crew of the "Penlee" lifeboat drowned as they battled in vain to save the crew of the coaster Union Star off Cornwall, England.
1984 - Britain and China signed an agreement for the return of Hong Kong to China in 1997.
1992 - South African President F.W. de Klerk said he had sacked or suspended 23 military officers including two generals for illegal and-or unauthorised activities and malpractices.
1993 - Two years after he was charged, a Pakistani court acquitted Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's husband, Asif Ali Zardari, of kidnapping.
1995 - Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky and his government, threatened by a looming budget row, tendered their resignations to President Thomas Klestil.
